law_name: Copyright Act, Cap. 300 (Copyright Act 1998, No. 4 of 1998; revised to 2006; amended by Act No. 17 of 2004)
term_of_protection: Author's life + 50 years (anonymous works publication + 50 years; audiovisual works creation/publication + 50 years)
author_rights: Exclusive right to reproduce, translate, adapt or arrange, and communicate the work to the public, or authorise others (s.10, subject to ss.24-29)
moral_rights: Right to claim authorship, to have it indicated, and to object to distortion, mutilation or derogatory treatment adversely affecting the author's character or reputation (s.11)
orphan_works: No general orphan-works rule. Minister may license reproduction of a published work when the reproduction-right owner is unknown, but only after three months (s.28, Second Schedule)
digital_protection: Barbados acceded to the WCT and WPPT effective 13 Dec 2019; their obligations were not yet incorporated into the 1998 Act (IIPA 2020 report)
fair_use_exceptions: Not a general fair-dealing clause. Permitted uses without consent (s.24(1)): personal use, quotations with source credit, teaching, news and press reporting, library copies
enforcement_body: Corporate Affairs and Intellectual Property Office (CAIPO)
notes: WPPT in force 13 December 2019 (WIPO notification, deposit 13 Sept 2019); WCT same period per Commons; Berne since 1983 and WTO since 1995 per Commons. WIPO Lex text seen is the 1982 Act; the 1998 Act text was not read.
